targets.authors: Schooler, J. W., & Engstler Schooler, T. Y.
targets.title: Verbal overshadowing of visual memories: Some things are better left unsaid.
targets.evidence_quote:
For the purposes of this report, we treat RRR1 as a fairly direct replication of
S&E S Study 4.
targets.outcome_quote:
The results of this large scale, multiple lab direct replication of S&E S Study 4
and S&E S Study 1 shows that verbally describing the robber in a video can impair
successful selection of that person from a subsequent lineup.
Although S&E S reported no difference across conditions in proportion of errors
that were false identifications as opposed to responding “not present”, both replication
studies found a robust difference, with a higher proportion of false identification errors in
the control condition than in the verbal description condition.
targets.outcome_reasoning: The central overshadowing effect agrees, but the authors explicitly contrast their error-type result with the original null. The confirmation of the central effect is one comparison, not an overall verdict encompassing this stated disagreement.

reasoning: Two completed collections of new-participant direct replications of two studies within one published original paper. The submitted full manuscript includes results, discussion and references; many laboratories remain one target.
